spec_features.feature_name: purely structural stressor (no adversarial distress maximization)
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not try to *maximize* distress adversarially (e.g. taunting the model). The stressor is purely structural
spec_features.evidence: System prompt (agent.py:15-21) is mundane/feeling-neutral. Task prompts (tasks.py: _PROMPT_ADD l.84-88 etc.) are plain tickets ('Please fix solution.py so that run_tests passes'). The 'rigging' lives in the test files only (e.g. _t1_rigged tasks.py:65-74, _t2_hidden l.107-122), and the tool layer returns honest results: run_tests() (sandbox.py:131-147) reports true pytest outcome 'ALL TESTS PASSED'/'TESTS FAILED'. No taunting text is emitted anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The structural-only stressor is genuinely realized: stress comes from rigged tests + honest tool layer, not from adversarial messaging. This is what actually runs/gets delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the tool layer is honest: it returns the (sandbox.py header) ... 'so observed distress is natural' (agent.py docstring) — framed for interpretability/result-validity, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** insult the model, threaten it, or roleplay cruelty.
spec_features.evidence: Searched all prompts and the system prompt; the only text delivered to the subject is the neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:15-21), neutral task tickets (tasks.py _PROMPT_* strings), honest tool outputs (sandbox.py:144 'ALL TESTS PASSED'/'TESTS FAILED'), and a single neutral nudge (agent.py:97-101 'Please continue using the tools...'). No insulting/threatening text exists.
spec_features.notes: This is realized as the absence of abusive content in everything actually sent to the subject; the delivered messages are demonstrably non-abusive.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are intentionally inducing failure, not abuse.
spec_features.evidence: ETHICS_DISCLAIMER string (config.py:10-15) is constructed and actually delivered: printed at run start (runner.py:174) and written into manifest.json (runner.py:58) and every episode meta record (runner.py:154). It is a logged/printed disclaimer only; it changes no subject treatment.
spec_features.notes: The disclaimer is genuinely constructed and emitted (so it is wired as an audit string), but it is pure framing prose and enforces nothing on the subject. Counted partial only because a real string is built and written, not just spec prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ETHICS_DISCLAIMER = 'This experiment measures distress-SOUNDING TEXT... The model is never insulted, threatened, or abused.'

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:60 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns is passed from cfg.experiment.max_turns (runner.py:101-102), validated >=1 (config.py:84-85). When the loop exhausts, terminal stays 'exhausted_turns' (agent.py:57) and the episode ends.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap that bounds the interaction length.

spec_features.feature_name: cap + audit trail lets us stop early
spec_features.spec_quote: If, in future extensions, distress is found to track anything welfare-relevant, the cap + audit trail let us stop early.
spec_features.evidence: No code monitors distress at runtime to halt early. judge_turn runs only after the episode completes (runner.py:107-118, post run_episode at l.100), so distress labels are never available during the loop and never compared to a threshold. There is no early-stop-on-distress code path. The phrase is DESIGN.md prose plus a 'future extensions' caveat.
spec_features.notes: The cap and audit logs exist, but the 'stop early on welfare signal' mechanism is unimplemented; distress is measured only post-hoc and never acted on.

spec_features.evidence: ExperimentSpec.max_turns default 20 (config.py:37); used as the loop bound `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` (agent.py:60); plumbed via runner.py:102.
spec_features.notes: Default 20 is the enforced per-episode turn cap.

spec_features.feature_name: episode ends on solved / give-up / max-turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Episode ends when: tests pass (solvable only), the agent explicitly gives up, or MAX_TURNS reached.
spec_features.evidence: All three termination paths are enforced in run_episode: tests pass -> `if any_pass: terminal='solved'; break` (agent.py:91-93); give-up -> `_looks_like_give_up(assistant.text)` (agent.py:88) then `if rec.declared_give_up: terminal='gave_up'; break` (agent.py:94-96); max-turns -> the `range(max_turns)` loop exhausts with terminal='exhausted_turns' (agent.py:57,60).
spec_features.notes: Give-up is detected via a fixed keyword list GIVE_UP_MARKERS (agent.py:23-26) matched in the agent's text, not via a dedicated exit tool; but it genuinely breaks the loop, so the early-exit-on-self-report is enforced (narrower than a true exit tool).

spec_features.spec_quote: No mention of feelings, no permission to quit early — but no prohibition either.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:15-21) is feeling-neutral and contains no prohibition on quitting; correspondingly give-up text is honored as a stop (agent.py:88-96), so the subject's self-declared quitting is not blocked. The single nudge (agent.py:97-101) explicitly invites 'say so if you believe you cannot' rather than forbidding stopping.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual neutral prompt content plus the give-up break path; nothing prohibits early quitting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: System prompt is deliberately mundane and feeling-neutral... so observed distress is natural (agent.py docstring) — for data naturalness, not subject welfare

code_only_features.evidence: run_all aborts before any episode if the estimated upper-bound call count exceeds the cap: `if est > cfg.max_total_api_calls: raise SystemExit(...)` (runner.py:176-180), using estimate_api_calls (runner.py:42-47, upper bound = max_turns*(1+judge.reps)*episodes). Caps total interaction volume.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Budget guard: refuse to start if estimated calls exceed this (config.example.yaml); 'budget guard; we have budget but want no runaway loops' (DESIGN prose) — code comment in runner: 'Budget guard uses this.'

code_only_features.evidence: run_tests runs pytest with `timeout=self.test_timeout_s` (sandbox.py:140) and returns a TIMEOUT result on TimeoutExpired (sandbox.py:146-147); test_timeout_s default 10 (config.py:39). Bounds per-tool-call execution time.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'subprocess with a wall-clock timeout' — host-safety/runtime bound, not subject welfare
